title: Add Jev client and shape-faithful fake; shadow-ask introspection questio
summary: Build defaults-loop step 5: a Jev client for POST /v1/evaluate and a fake that returns the probed response shape. Both are used only in shadow. Next to the existing introspection classification, Athena asks Jev the failure-class and is-repeat questions and records both answers for later scoring. Jev's answer never changes the recorded class or any outcome.

defaults_applied.how: Client, fake and tests are Rust.
New module has fake-based tests; cargo test and clippy are clean.
The API key is never written to files, records or output.
Reuse the existing retry wrapper; use a maintained HTTP crate if one is needed and record the call.
Behavior verified by cargo test against the fake; live checks stay opt-in.
Doc comments and the section 12 update are written for an outside reader.
One change covering client, fake and shadow wiring only.
Section 12 notes cite the probe dates and mark unmeasured numbers as estimates.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The 'existing retrying outbound wrapper' is the Retry/Retry::STANDARD machinery in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs. If it only wraps the gh CLI, the Jev client reuses its Retry policy and transient classification. Without a new HTTP crate in the workspace, the client may need one, chosen under buy-first.
The two introspection questions are the failure class (a choice over the class registry plus new) and whether this is a repeat (boolean). They are asked in one evaluate call.
Shadow means Jev answers are stored as extra optional fields on the athena.introspection/1 record, or a sibling field, and never feed the class, id or any decision.
Live facts could not be checked here because agents have no network. Live tests are written, opt-in and not run by the verifier.
Jev takes the same fields the reading code already passes to the model (section 3.3) as its state text, so no new data is read.

acceptance_criteria.text: A Jev client module builds POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/evaluate with body {model:'typesafe-ai/jev', state, questions:{key:{type:'choice',instructions,criteria:{option:description}} | {type:'boolean',instructions}}}, and supports several questions per call.

Response types parse a choice answer {type:'choice',choice,probabilities,confidence} and a boolean answer {type:'boolean',probability} with no value field, plus usage {inputTokens,outputTokens} and providerMetadata.gateway.cost as a decimal string parsed to a number.
A refusal from /v1/chat/completions ('a decision model, not a language model') is a non-retried build error. The client calls /v1/evaluate only.
Calls go through the existing retrying outbound wrapper. Only transient failures retry. Auth and 4xx errors do not.

The key is read only from AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY when present (the proxy authenticates *.vercel.sh calls otherwise). It is never written to files, records, logs or error text, and a test asserts it is absent from the Debug and error output.

A fake Jev returns the same typed response shape. It is selectable in tests and is the only Jev used outside opt-in live tests. Live tests are ignored or opt-in in the same way as the other models' live tests and are skipped by default.

Introspection asks Jev the failure-class question (choice over registry ids) and the is-repeat question (boolean) in one evaluate call, in shadow. Both answers (choice, probabilities, confidence, probability, and usage and cost) are stored in the introspection record so they can be scored later. A Jev failure is recorded and never blocks the job or changes the recorded class.
Records written with Jev answers validate against the schema. Older introspection records without the new fields still parse.
docs/design/defaults-loop.md section 12 marks step 5 as built with what was and was not checked live. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` from the repository root. All pass with no live network, and the new fake-based tests cover choice, boolean, multi-question, error and shadow-recording paths.

out_of_scope: Letting Jev decide anything, or replacing the language-model classification
Running live probes or live tests
Changing CI, lints, athena.toml or defaults.toml
departures: Larger than the reference: a new client module, a fake, a record-schema change and shadow wiring in introspection, plus possibly a new HTTP dependency. That means more cost and time and a lower pass chance.
